_comment: Q7 SSOT. Closed-vocabulary map from a DESIGNED kind (the designer's starter-partial
vocabulary) to the kit-native widget that realises it.
VOCABULARY SOURCE: skills/appbox-designer/starter-partials/widgets/_<kind>.tsx — the file
list IS the vocabulary. Derive it (strip leading _ and .tsx); never hand-maintain a copy.
Every kind in that directory must appear in `kinds` — as a `widget`, or as a `composedFrom`
recipe or `presentation` mode when no single kit class realises it. Coverage: 15/15.
v1.1.0 did NOT add missing kinds — v1.0.0 already covered all 15. It fixed a real defect:
`composedFrom` and `presentation` were absent from `resolution.order`, so the two kinds
using them (panel-activity, modal) would have fallen through to FAIL despite being
correctly authored. A reachability bug, not a coverage bug. See scripts/validate-registry.py.
v1.2.0 added the Q12 inspect identity: `designVocabulary.inspectAttrs` (the Dart shape's
one home, in kit core) and `anatomyNodes` (the closed anatomy-node-id vocabulary). It added
no kinds and changed no resolution. See the `anatomyNodes._comment` for why that set has
exactly one member today — it is small because it is honest, not because it is unfinished.
Widget names below were enumerated from kit/ui_library/lib — they are real classes, not
invented placeholders. The scaffolder resolves through this table and NOWHERE else.
CORE RULE (Q7): an unresolvable kind is a FAIL that names the kind and the design node.
There is no silent Container fallback. A silent fallback produces a scaffold that compiles,
looks plausible and is wrong — the exact failure the whole gate stack exists to prevent.

resolution.nullWidgetRule: Three entry shapes resolve with widget:null, and ALL THREE must be named in `order` — a shape that is not listed falls through to FAIL, silently turning a designed kind into a build break. (1) `composedFrom`: no single kit class realises the kind; the scaffolder emits the listed classes explicitly as a composition and NEVER collapses them to one class. (2) `presentation`: the kind is a route/overlay presentation mode, not a subtree; the scaffolder sets the flag and hosts via the named service. (3) `variants`: the widget depends on a variant key. Adding a fourth shape means adding a line to `order` in the same edit.

failureContract.messageTemplate: unresolvable kind '<kind>' at design node <anatomyNodeId> (surface <surfaceId>): not in kind-resolution.registry.json v<registryVersion>

escapeHatch.rule: Trail-leaving, never silent. An escape entry emits the widget AND a build-time warning naming the reason and owner. An expired escape is a FAIL.
escapeHatch.rationale: Escapes are how a real design ships before the kit catches up; making them loud and dated stops them becoming permanent.

appbar.note: This kind resolves top chrome the DESIGN declared; it never adds chrome a surface's anatomy is silent about (chrome-scoping ruling, 2026-08-13). Resolution table, per surface: (1) design declares shell/tab-root top chrome -> `shell` variant, AppBoxKitChromeScaffold, THE liquid-glass law's reuse unit (docs/liquid-glass-allowlist.md; ratified 2026-08-13), which carries the runtime tier branch (Liquid Glass floating chrome / Android M3E boxed / fallback boxed) so emitted code never hand-assembles Scaffold.appBar next to in-scroll native glass; (2) pushed surface whose scroll content holds native glass -> `shell` variant too, since the floating-back-affordance ruling (2026-08-13) gave the scaffold a `leading` slot (leading: back); (3) pushed surface with Flutter-only scroll content -> the bare `widget`; (4) surface designed with NO top chrome -> nothing at all, which is lawful output rather than a gap — there is deliberately no variant key for this case, because a resolver must emit nothing, not something. Chrome is per surface: a surface hosting a nested router must not carry chrome its pushed routes would inherit (the double-bar stack). Per target the assembly standard differs — iOS/macOS liquid-glass law, Android M3E law (docs/m3e-law.md), web/desktop their own conventions.

empty-state.note: NO single kit widget realises this kind. It is a COMPOSITION, and the scaffolder emits the composition explicitly rather than resolving to one class. Recorded here so `empty-state` is inside the closed vocabulary and never trips the unresolvable-kind FAIL.

note: Q7 reconciliation: `modal` is a distinct DESIGNED kind (authored partial), NOT a dialog
variant and NOT a vocabulary deletion. It resolves to a PRESENTATION MODE, not a widget
subtree: the scaffolder sets the route presentation flag and hosts the surface via the
overlay service. `dialog` remains a separate kind.
What separates them in the design is DATA FRESHNESS, not form: _modal.tsx is a
zero-request <details> toggle over content the page already holds; _dialog.tsx is a
server-swapped <dialog> for content fetched fresh. That axis is a web-transport concern
with no widget analogue, so it does not survive transliteration at the widget layer —
it re-appears one layer up, in the viewmodel binding (modal binds a value the surface
already has; dialog binds an async source).
Why NOT AppBoxKitFrostedAlertDialog: its constructor REQUIRES title, message and a
List<AppBoxKitNativeDialogAction>. _modal has no action contract — only a close X and a
caller-supplied body. Resolving there would invent buttons the design never authored,
which is exactly the plausible-but-wrong scaffold this registry exists to prevent.

panel-activity.note: Q7 reconciliation: COMPOSITION — no first-class kit activity widget exists yet; this entry is a recorded debt pending one. Compositions are designer RECIPES: the designer always composes panels for any design; the scaffolder emits the composition explicitly, never resolves to one class.
panel-activity.debt: Replace with first-class kit activity widget when available.

tabbar.note: tab:true registry entries compile to AppBoxKitBottomNavScaffold at the shell level; this kind is the in-surface tab strip. The BAR only — the panel/stack it drives is the sibling kind `tabs`, which owns AppBoxKitAnimatedTabStack outright. Do not re-add that class as a companion here; it was deliberately promoted out.

tabs.note: Q7 reconciliation: promoted from tabbar.companions to primary target. `tabbar` is the in-surface tab strip; `tabs` is the animated tabbed content stack. Two authored partials (_tabs.tsx, _tabbar.tsx), two kinds, two widgets — a design may use either alone, so neither may be folded into the other.

supportKinds._comment: Non-visual kit primitives the scaffolder wires structurally. Not part of the designed kind vocabulary; listed so emitted scaffolds reference real classes.

designVocabulary._comment: Q6 Tier 1. Colors, spacing, glyphs and fonts resolve to kit-core common — NEVER to a generated local file. Enforced by feature-recipe.manifest.json#/kitCommonImports/forbiddenLocalDuplicates.

_comment: Q12 SSOT. The CLOSED vocabulary of anatomy-node ids — the third slot of the inspect
identity triple (screenId, surfaceId, anatomyNodeId). Ratified at registry v1.2.0;
second member ratified by the user at v1.3.0.
SHAPE: the Dart type is AppBoxKitInspectAttrs, and it lives in exactly one place —
designVocabulary.inspectAttrs above. The scaffolder imports it; it NEVER re-emits the
class into a generated app. A shape re-emitted per app is a shape that drifts per app.
SPELLING: the JS form at skills/appbox-designer/references/app-architecture.md:169 names
this key `nodeId`; Dart names it `anatomyNodeId` (skills/appbox-scaffolder/SKILL.md:263).
One slot, two spellings, deliberately recorded here so neither reads as a defect.
WHY THE SET HAS TWO MEMBERS: 'anatomy:view.body' was derived, not authored — closing the
set at what actually exists is the point; inventing widget-level or slot-level ids to make
the vocabulary look complete would make any probe that checks output against it a tautology.
'anatomy:shell.surface' was ratified by the user at v1.3.0 (Q11 spike follow-up): six
screenIds were each carried by two files — the shell frame and its leaf — and a one-member
vocabulary could not tell them apart. The spelling mirrors view.body's region.part form and
draws on authored prose ('Shell-level surfaces sit one level up', app-architecture.md:138;
showcase-anatomy.md: 'A shell's own surface sits one level up, beside its children').
The set grows the same way a widget kind grows: deliberately, in one edit, with a version bump.
CONSEQUENCE, restated: within one screenId, anatomyNodeId now distinguishes the shell frame
('anatomy:shell.surface') from the view body ('anatomy:view.body'); sibling surfaces are
still told apart by surfaceId.

vocabulary.anatomy:view.body: The root body node of a view — the subtree a surface's build() returns. Every emitted leaf view and every back-stamped showcase leaf view carries this id.
vocabulary.anatomy:shell.surface: The shell-level surface — the frame a shell contributes one level up, beside its children. Carried by the seven *_shell_view.dart frame views; ratified at v1.3.0 to resolve the frame/leaf screenId collision.

failureContract.messageTemplate: unknown anatomy-node id '<anatomyNodeId>' (surface <surfaceId>): not in kind-resolution.registry.json#/anatomyNodes/vocabulary v<registryVersion>
failureContract.rule: An anatomy-node id outside this set is a gate failure on BOTH sides — designer and scaffolder — exactly as an unmapped widget kind is. Never improvise one, and never widen the set to make a failing run pass; widening is a deliberate registry change with a version bump.
forbidden: inferring the node from the widget tree at runtime
defaulting to 'anatomy:view.body' for a node that is not a view body
emitting an empty or null anatomyNodeId

sharedWith.appbox-designer: The designer resolves the SAME table when choosing starter partials, so a designed kind and a scaffolded widget cannot disagree. Divergence between the two skills' copies is a defect; there is exactly one file.
